item.title: Blinken warns US ground invasion of Iran would be 'absolute disaster' as Tehran escalates attacks
item.description: Former Secretary of State Antony Blinken warned a U.S. ground invasion of Iran would be an "absolute disaster" as Tehran launched drones at Bahrain.
item.content:encoded:
Former Secretary of State Antony Blinken warned Saturday that airstrikes alone may not eliminate Iran's weapons capabilities, but said a U.S. ground invasion would be an "absolute disaster."

Speaking at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi, Blinken, who served under President Biden, pointed to Iran's massive territory, population of roughly 90 million and ability to produce weapons deep inside the country as obstacles to any military campaign aimed at dismantling its arsenal.

"The weapons that it continues to produce are back far enough, the range is great enough that you can't just take everything out," Blinken said. "You'd probably have to have a land invasion of some kind to do that, which would be an absolute disaster."

TRUMP KEEPS SIGNALING AN END TO IRAN WAR, BUT EXPERT WARNS A CRUCIAL PIECE OF HIS STRATEGY IS MISSING

Blinken's warning came ahead of Iran claiming Sunday to have launched six drones at a U.S. military installation in Bahrain, while reports surfaced that neighboring Iraq faced concerns that its territory could be drawn into a potential American ground operation.

Bahrain said its air defenses blocked several Iranian aerial attacks Sunday, the first such interceptions since September.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it targeted a U.S. air defense radar system at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base with six drones in retaliation for what it described as "hostile US actions," according to Iranian state media, Reuters reported.

Bahraini officials said the drones were intercepted before reaching their targets.

IRAN HAS 'SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASED' EFFORTS TO TARGET AMERICANS ABROAD, US INTELLIGENCE MEMO WARNS

The latest escalation came amid further fighting in Yemen, where the Houthis made advances against Saudi-backed forces, raising additional concerns about the conflict spreading across the region.

Blinken warned that Iran retains the ability to widen the confrontation despite the United States' overwhelming conventional military superiority.

While Washington can "escalate vertically" by intensifying its bombing campaign, Blinken said, Tehran can "escalate horizontally" by targeting American military installations, regional allies and critical infrastructure, either directly or through allied armed groups.

"Even though we're much more powerful, that asymmetry in their ability to escalate horizontally as opposed to vertically is not to our advantage," Blinken said.

The former top diplomat also emphasized the geographic challenges facing U.S. forces.

"That coastline along the Strait of Hormuz goes on forever," Blinken said.

Iran is roughly four times the size of California, with a coastline and weapons production facilities that could complicate efforts to eliminate its military capabilities through air power alone.

TRUMP'S MOAB THREAT COULD PUT IRAN'S DEEPEST BUNKERS IN AMERICA'S CROSSHAIRS

Concerns about a potential ground operation have also intensified in neighboring Iraq, where officials have resisted proposals to sharply restrict trade and movement across the Iranian border.

Iran International reported that Tehran has become concerned that Iraqi territory could be used as a staging ground for a potential U.S. operation into southern Iran.

The Iraqi newspaper Al-Mada reported Nov. 9 that Iraq's prime minister privately briefed Shiite political leaders on an alleged American military plan involving a ground offensive, the outlet said.

In an interview with France 24 published Friday, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein had also warned that the region's unstable security environment could not continue indefinitely.

The current state of "no war and no peace" is unsustainable, Hussein said, warning that the confrontation "either goes towards peace or it goes towards war."

AFTER 47 YEARS OF CONFRONTING IRAN, DOES AMERICA HAVE A STRATEGY FOR ENDING THIS WAR?

Hussein also said Baghdad has a responsibility to pursue diplomatic mediation because Iraq has already been drawn into the conflict.

He pointed to recent outreach to Tehran, including discussions with Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.

The Iraqi foreign minister also rejected a reported U.S. demand that Baghdad close all but two of its land border crossings with Iran, describing the proposed restrictions as "not possible" and "a kind of sanction against the Iraqi people."

The border dispute comes as U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) expands efforts to disrupt Iranian weapons shipments and illicit trade through Task Force Iron Gate.

CENTCOM announced the task force would coordinate with other U.S. agencies to prevent Iran from transporting advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials and illicit revenue across its land borders and the Caspian Sea.

Iraq shares a roughly 1,000-mile border with Iran.

item.title: TikToker arrested after big cat mauls teen to death during video shoot at private farm
item.description: A TikToker and farm owner were arrested after a big cat fatally mauled a teenage worker during a video shoot in Pakistan, Lahore officials said.
item.content:encoded:
A TikToker has been arrested alongside a farm owner after a big cat viciously mauled a teenage employee to death during a video shoot in eastern Pakistan, officials said Thursday.

The attack happened at a private breeding farm near Kahna, according to The Times of India.

The animal "got out of control in the presence of the TikToker, who had come to the farmhouse to make a TikTok video, leaving a farm employee critically injured," Lahore police said in a post on X.

Although police described the animal as a lioness, a photo shared by the agency alongside its statement appeared to show a tiger.

'LOOKSMAXXING' INFLUENCER CLAVICULAR CHARGED AFTER ALLEGEDLY SHOOTING DEAD ALLIGATOR ON LIVESTREAM

The victim, 19, was identified as Talha, while the arrested farm owner was identified as Fayyaz and the TikToker as Noman, according to The Times of India. 

The outlet added that the TikToker had reportedly asked for the animal to be released from its enclosure for a TikTok video shoot.

After the attack, Talha was rushed to a private hospital but died while undergoing treatment.

**GRAPHIC WARNING**

NEARLY 100 MONKEYS ESCAPE ENCLOSURE, INVADE NEIGHBORHOODS AS OFFICIALS SCRAMBLE TO RECAPTURE THEM

Police opened a case into the incident and uncovered an alleged attempt to "conceal the truth."

"An attempt was made to pass off the lioness attack as a dog attack," police said.

Investigators are examining whether the farm had the proper permits to keep the big cat, whether adequate safety measures were in place and whether negligence played a role in the attack.

The animal involved has also been handed over to wildlife authorities.

item.title: NTSB details warning whistles and emergency orders before tanker collision capsized New Orleans riverboat
item.description: NTSB investigators detail warning whistles and emergency orders captured on the tanker's voyage recorder before the New Orleans riverboat collision.
item.content:encoded:
A tanker suffered a steering problem about two minutes before slamming into a docked New Orleans riverboat Friday, federal investigators said Sunday, detailing warning whistles, calls for help and emergency orders before the collision.

The Atlantic Asphalt was heading upriver near the Crescent City Connection Bridge at about 12:26 p.m. when its rudder remained turned to the right, sending the ship toward the Mississippi River’s east bank, National Transportation Safety Board senior marine accident investigator Bart Barnum said.

The tanker struck American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage at about 12:28 p.m. The riverboat capsized in about 22 minutes, according to preliminary information presented by the NTSB.

NEW ORLEANS BOAT CRASH CALLED ‘MIRACLE ON THE MISSISSIPPI’ AS EVERYONE IS ACCOUNTED FOR, OFFICIALS SAY

Investigators downloaded more than nine hours of data from the tanker’s voyage data recorder, including bridge audio, rudder angle, engine RPM, course and speed.

The recordings captured sounds consistent with the ship’s whistle, warnings and requests for assistance over its marine radio, commands to deploy anchors and emergency shiphandling orders, Barnum said.

11-NIGHT CARIBBEAN CRUISE ABRUPTLY CANCELED AFTER COAST GUARD DETAINS SHIP

Officials described the steering problem as a "steering casualty," but cautioned that the term does not establish what went wrong.

"It could be many different things. That is something that we are investigating very closely," Barnum said.

AT LEAST 6 PEOPLE INJURED AFTER BOSTON DUCK BOAT OVERTURNS NEAR ENTRANCE TO POPULAR TOURIST ATTRACTION

NTSB board member John DeLeeuw said investigators have data on the tanker’s speed but are still analyzing it before releasing it publicly. Video showed anchors were down, but investigators are still determining which ones were deployed and how far, he said.

The findings follow a frantic rescue effort that officials said left everyone aboard the American Heritage alive. Roughly 100 people were pulled from the Mississippi River, while responders evacuated more than 80 before the vessel overturned, Port of New Orleans Harbor Police Chief Melanie Montroll said Saturday.

TWO DEAD, INCLUDING INFANT, AFTER BOAT CAPSIZES IN NEW YORK HARBOR; 12 RESCUED

"This is a miracle. It is a literal miracle on the Mississippi," Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry said Friday.

Eight people remained hospitalized Saturday, including two in serious condition. The other six were stable, officials said.

FBI INVESTIGATES SUSPECTED HOMICIDE ABOARD MSC SEASCAPE CRUISE SHIP AFTER SUDDEN RETURN TO TEXAS

The NTSB said Sunday that 140 passengers and 50 crew members were aboard the riverboat, a total of 190.

New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno also said the American Heritage’s captain was injured but stayed aboard until passengers and crew were accounted for, becoming the last person to leave.

MOM LOSES GRIP ON DAUGHTER AS PASSENGER FERRY CAPSIZES WITH 20 PEOPLE STILL MISSING

"Every moment of the critical time [Friday], he did not want to leave his ship," Moreno said Saturday.

Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham said Saturday that crews were preparing to remove 16,000 gallons of fuel before salvage operations, warning that removing the capsized vessel could take weeks. DeLeeuw said Sunday that divers had been in the water, with salvage work overseen by the Coast Guard and salvage companies.

UNLICENSED NYC BOAT OPERATOR ALLEGEDLY IGNORED SAFETY WARNINGS BEFORE MOTHER, BABY DIED IN CAPSIZING: FEDS

Interviews with American Heritage crew members were underway Sunday. Interviews with the Atlantic Asphalt’s crew were scheduled to begin Monday and continue through the week, Barnum said.

The NTSB expects to release a preliminary report within about 30 days. Sunday’s briefing was its last planned on-site news conference, DeLeeuw said, with further updates to be posted online.

Fox News Digital's Brittany Miller contributed to this report.

item.title: Ashley Judd claims mom Naomi threatened to pull tuition over what she was learning and her lesbian professor
item.description: Ashley Judd reveals Naomi Judd threatened to stop paying her tuition over a lesbian theologian professor on her new podcast "A Table Prepared."
item.content:encoded:
Ashley Judd is opening up about a past rift with her late mother, Naomi Judd, sparked by a lesbian college professor.

On the debut episode of her new podcast, "A Table Prepared," Ashley sat down with her co-host, former Christ Church Nashville Pastor Dan Scott. During their conversation, Ashley claimed that Naomi "threatened to stop paying my tuition at the University of Kentucky" over what she was learning, and also the professor's sexual orientation. 

"She didn’t like what I was learning," Ashley said. "She didn’t like [that] I had a lesbian theologian professor that was taking me through Hebrew scripture and looking at the women listed as property after the donkeys."

Ashley explained that her mother, who died by suicide in 2022, felt pressured to align politically with the country music industry out of fear of "disapproval and retaliation." Behind closed doors, however, Naomi was much more open about expressing her personal and political beliefs "in the home."

WYNONNA JUDD WISHES BOND WITH MOM WAS LIKE THEIR MUSIC, BUT 'THERE WAS A LOT OF DYSFUNCTION'

"She could share all kinds of political and social views that would surprise people if they thought Naomi Judd thought, felt, said that," Ashley said.

As an example of the issues that moved her mother, Ashley noted that Naomi felt "a lot of compassion" for women making headlines for harming their children.

"She would say they need help, not punishment," Ashley recalled, adding that she wasn't sure if Naomi "would have been comfortable in her lifetime saying that."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"I’ve debated with myself, is it okay for me to say that posthumously and attribute it to her? I’m still in relationship with my mother, and so I’ve asked her these things," Ashley said. "I was up the other morning … and the part of my mother that lives in me said, ‘Honey, I told stories. You tell the truth.'"

In that moment, Ashley said she felt her mother had "passed [the] baton."

Country music icon Naomi Judd died by suicide on April 30, 2022, at the age of 76, from a self-inflicted gunshot wound at her home near Franklin, Tennessee, where Ashley discovered her body.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Her passing followed years of openly documented battles with severe, treatment-resistant depression, bipolar disorder, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress, which she detailed in her 2016 memoir, "River of Time."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Tragedy struck just one day before she and her daughter Wynonna Judd were officially inducted as The Judds into the Country Music Hall of Fame. At the family's request, her daughters still attended the ceremony after releasing a statement noting they had lost their mother to "the disease of mental illness."

Following her death, Judd's husband of 32 years, Larry Strickland, and her daughters successfully petitioned a Tennessee court to seal the police investigation records and autopsy photos to protect their family's privacy.

item.title: Kirk Cousins and the Minnesota Vikings are reunited and it feels so good after win over Green Bay Packers
item.description: Kirk Cousins led the Minnesota Vikings to a dominant win at Lambeau Field, and his emotional reunion with Kevin O'Connell raises a big question.
item.content:encoded:
We found out a lot about Kirk Cousins and the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday because it is hard to add a new quarterback on a Tuesday, have him in full practices only two days during the week, and by week's end win a game in the same venue where he tore his Achilles three years ago.

All that happened Sunday when the Minnesota Vikings beat the Green Bay Packers.

But of all the things we learned from this game, maybe the most important is that Cousins and the Vikings maybe should not have broken up a couple of years ago.

Perhaps they shouldn't have gone looking for greener pastures, shouldn't have believed for better outcomes, should not have quit on each other and the pretty good thing they had.

VIKINGS ACQUIRE KIRK COUSINS FROM RAIDERS WHO TURN TO FERNANDO MENDOZA AS THEIR STARTING QB

The Vikings and Cousins are together again. They're reunited and after winning in Lambeau Field, and they both feel so good.

"It's been a blast to do ball with him again," coach Kevin O'Connell said afterward.

"Football's an emotional game, and my football journey goes way back, and, you know, there's been highs and lows," Cousins told reporters after the victory. "And there's more of the story to write up ahead, but the last three years since being here have been a tough three years.

"And, there's a lot of gratitude right now for being in this group again."

The story of the misguided direction perhaps began in 2023 when Cousins tore his Achilles at Lambeau Field. Unable to overcome the injury by delivering a good season in 2026, the Vikings and Cousins went their different directions in March of 2024.

Cousins went to the Atlanta Falcons as a high-priced free agent, believing he could ultimately finish his career there. But that changed weeks after signing him, the Falcons drafted Michael Penix Jr. in the first round of the draft and anointed the rookie their starter before that very season was over.

Cousins sat much of 2025, and then went to the Raiders last offseason knowing he was keeping the starter's seat warm for Fernando Mendoza. Little did he know that seat would be pulled out from under him last week.

MINNESOTA VIKINGS' SOFT BENCHING OF KYLER MURRAY LEADS TO CARSON WENTZ TAKING OVER AS NEW STARTING QB

The Vikings? They didn't move on from Cousins to live happily ever after.

When Cousins left in 2024, the Vikings thought replacing him wasn't an issue. They had found Sam Darnold in 2024, they were getting ready to draft J.J. McCarthy in the first round, and there was a certain arrogance within the organization that they could find someone, anyone, and turn him into a treasure.

VIKINGS QUARTERBACK BATTLE MEETS EXPECTED END AS KYLER MURRAY BEATS OUT JJ MCCARTHY FOR STARTING JOB

But then Darnold left. And McCarthy didn't work out. And Carson Wentz didn't work out, and Kyler Murray didn't work out earlier this season.

And after those missteps, the Vikings decided last week that Cousins was their best option once again – just as he'd been from 2018 to 2023.

And Cousin showed he's all of that in this one game.

Cousins was already an upgrade by the time the Vikings held a 20-0 lead in the third quarter and scored twice more when the Packers tried to rally.

And, yes, we know ... That is not exactly Super Bowl caliber quarterback play we saw from Cousins, because he did throw an interception and he still has to clean up some stuff.

But having Cousins at quarterback clearly raised the Vikings' hopes. Justin Jefferson played with energy again. The offense could run the ball better because the Packers had to respect the passing game.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

And the defense that is among the best in the NFL sacked Jordan Love eight times – the most by any team in a game this season – because the unit was in the mostly unfamiliar spot of playing with a lead.

"I thought for one of the first times this year, we played complimentary football," O'Connell said.

Cousins was careful when it was over to remind everyone that the story of his return and this Vikings' season is not fully written. But we have a good start to the tale:

It begins with the fact this combination maybe would have been better off staying together.

item.title: TNA's Trey Miguel working his way to Canada for Destination X title match despite travel chaos
item.description: Trey Miguel's TNA World Championship match against Leon Slater was in jeopardy after Friday's nationwide ground stop stranded him in transit.
item.content:encoded:
Trey Miguel worked hard to earn a Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA) World Championship opportunity at Destination X and Friday’s nationwide ground stop added to the obstacles.

For a real moment, it appeared Miguel wasn’t going to make it to Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, for the match Sunday night against Leon Slater.

As the minutes crept closer, Miguel was still not at the Edmonton Expo Centre.

Miguel won a ladder match to earn the chance at Leon Slater’s world title. He’s stayed off social media for the most part as he worked his way to The Great White North.

The world title match was far from the only one in jeopardy. Multiple pro wrestlers were unable to get to Edmonton for the pay-per-view.

TNA president Carlos Silva announced Saturday there would be some changes to the card as travel issues persisted through the weekend.

item.title: USC great Keyshawn Johnson calls for Lincoln Riley's job: 'Time to find somebody else'
item.description: Keyshawn Johnson posted a frustrated video calling for USC to fire Lincoln Riley after the Trojans' 27-13 loss to Indiana knocked them from CFP contention.
item.content:encoded:
The No. 18 USC Trojans would’ve helped their College Football Playoff chances if they could take down No. 9 Indiana on the road Saturday, but they were unable to muster second-half points in a 27-13 defeat.

Now, one Trojan legend is calling for head coach Lincoln Riley to be fired.

Keyshawn Johnson, the former wide receiver who went on to become a Super Bowl winner and three-time Pro Bowler in the NFL, posted a video on X where he was very frustrated with the result in Bloomington.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"I tried my best, but in all honesty, though, it’s time to – you know what I mean? It’s just time to find somebody else," he said in the video.

"I’m sorry, man. I don’t even know what to say. Where did we go wrong here? It’s unbelievable. I just don’t even know what to say."

INDIANA HOOSIERS BOOST COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF HOPES WITH 27-13 WIN OVER USC TROJANS

Johnson added, "Fight On, I guess," but he isn’t in the biggest of USC spirits after the loss.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Things were going well in the game, as the Trojans and Hoosiers were tied at 10 apiece entering halftime. However, USC had just three points in the second half, while Indiana found their way to run away with it at home.

Riley and the Trojans were riding high after taking down Ohio State earlier this season, which propelled them upward in the CFP standings. They had the opportunity to continue moving up if they could pick up key wins along the way.

But this loss, which moved USC to 7-3 on the season, essentially knocks them out of contention for the CFP.

With yet another three-loss season at this point for Riley, the chatter will grow about his future with the program. In fact, it was already present before the Ohio State game began to change the conversation. That 30-18 victory at home had Trojans fans believing a late-season run could get them in position to get a chance to fight for a national title.

After Indiana, USC is set to face unranked Maryland, but they would’ve seen No. 4 UCLA in their final regular-season matchup, which had the chance to be a gamechanger.

Instead, USC is looking to finish the year strong now, and Riley, who was hired in November 2021, could be coaching his final games as the Trojans look ahead to next season.

item.title: Joe Biden calls Zelenskyy 'moody and stubborn,' questions his gratitude in new memoir
item.description: Joe Biden calls Volodymyr Zelenskyy "moody" and "not as grateful as I would have expected" in his forthcoming memoir, "Promise Me, America."
item.content:encoded:
Former President Joe Biden described Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as difficult in private and insufficiently grateful in a forthcoming memoir reviewed Friday by The Wall Street Journal, adding his assessment to a relationship President Donald Trump has also publicly criticized.

Zelenskyy "could be moody and stubborn in our private conversations, and not as grateful as I would have expected," Biden said in "Promise Me, America," according to the newspaper.

Zelenskyy previously addressed questions about his gratitude during a February 2025 interview with Fox News' Bret Baier on "Special Report," following his Oval Office clash with Trump and Vice President JD Vance. When Baier asked whether he owed Trump an apology, Zelenskyy emphasized his appreciation for American support.

"I'm thankful to President Trump and to Congress, bipartisan support, and I was always very thankful from all our people," Zelenskyy said.

TRUMP CALLS FOR UKRAINE TO REPLACE ZELENSKYY AFTER CLASH OVER RUSSIA DIESEL DEAL: 'GET A NEW PRESIDENT'

In a November interview with Fox News chief foreign correspondent Trey Yingst, Zelenskyy defended Ukraine’s strikes on Russian oil refineries despite objections from the Trump administration.

Biden’s memoir also addresses his handling of the presidential transition and his concerns about the incoming Trump administration’s approach to negotiations with Moscow.

According to the account, Trump’s team sought a letter authorizing direct negotiations with Russian President Vladimir Putin before Trump returned to office. Biden said he declined because of what he believed such talks could mean for Ukraine.

KUSHNER ENTERS UKRAINE PEACE TALKS AS TRUMP EYES SECURING SAFEGUARDS AGAINST ANOTHER RUSSIAN INVASION

He was "unwilling to give them carte blanche for what I expected would be a kind of surrender, at Ukraine's expense," Biden said.

The former president also offered a personal assessment of Putin’s behavior during their encounters, describing an effort to project disinterest.

Putin "liked to slouch during a meeting, feigning indifference, like a teenager," Biden said.

Biden’s criticism of Zelenskyy appears alongside a favorable assessment of the Ukrainian leader’s previous career. His acting background "turned out to be very good training," Biden said.

ZELENSKYY CAN LEVERAGE MOSCOW TIES FROM COMEDY DAYS TO MAKE PEACE DEAL, SAYS FORMER KEY AIDE

During Biden’s presidency, Ukraine’s requests included stronger air defenses, expanded weapons production and assistance disrupting Russian military logistics, according to a December 2023 account from Zelenskyy’s office. Before that White House meeting, Zelenskyy expressed appreciation for international assistance.

"I’d like to thank America and our partners for their support," Zelenskyy said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Biden subsequently announced additional assistance in September 2024, including $2.4 billion through the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative, another Patriot air defense battery and expanded training for Ukrainian F-16 pilots. His statement framed the measures as part of helping Ukraine defeat Russia’s invasion.

"The United States will provide Ukraine with the support it needs to win this war," Biden said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Zelenskyy for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: White House calls DC policies 'insanity' after 19-year-old gunman gets probation in shooting
item.description: A 19-year-old who prosecutors said fired more than 20 rounds into a D.C. neighborhood got probation, prompting the White House to slam the city's crime policies.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE – A 19-year-old who authorities say fired more than 20 rounds into a Washington, D.C., neighborhood and wounded a boy playing basketball has been released on probation, prompting the White House to denounce the city’s sentencing policies as "insanity."

Prosecutors wanted Darius Drew behind bars for five years. Instead, a judge suspended a two-year prison sentence and ordered 18 months of supervised probation under the Youth Rehabilitation Act, a D.C. law U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro had previously urged lawmakers to overhaul.

"The case illustrates the insanity of Washington, D.C.’s soft-on-crime policies that allow adults to receive just a slap on the wrist for dangerous crimes like firing twenty rounds of ammunition into the community," White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis told Fox News Digital.

TRUMP’S DC LAW-AND-ORDER BLITZ MARKS ONE YEAR WITH EYE-POPPING HAUL OF SUSPECTS

"It is remarkable that even with these types of radical policies in place, President Trump’s Safe and Beautiful Task Force has been able to drive down violent crime in our nation’s capital," Bis added.

Superior Court Judge Jennifer Di Toro granted Drew sentencing treatment under the Youth Rehabilitation Act over the government’s objection, according to federal prosecutors. Drew pleaded guilty Aug. 10 to aggravated assault and carrying a pistol without a license.

CHAOTIC TEEN BRAWL GOES VIRAL AFTER TEEN TERROR PROMPTS US ATTORNEY PIRRO'S PLAN TO PROSECUTE PARENTS

He was released Friday after spending nearly six months in custody following his May 22 arrest. Prosecutors opposed his release as well as the use of the youth sentencing law.

The gunfire that put him there came from two locations in a Northwest Washington neighborhood, according to the government’s evidence.

MARYLAND MAN ACCUSED OF GIRL'S FATAL SHOOTING RELEASED FROM PRISON DAYS BEFORE

On May 11, Drew rode a Lime bike into an alley before surveillance video captured him firing at a parked car, prosecutors said. The ShotSpotter gunfire detection system registered 10 shots.

Seconds later, Drew fired toward a nearby house. A boy playing basketball at a recreation center was struck in the leg.

By the time the shooting stopped, Drew had fired more than 20 rounds into the community, prosecutors said. Investigators later found two firearms, ammunition and large amounts of suspected narcotics and marijuana at his home.

REPEAT OFFENDER ACCUSED OF SHOOTING NATIONAL GUARD MEMBER HAS LENGTHY HISTORY WITH THE LAW, RECORDS SHOW

The probation ruling echoes a warning Pirro delivered to the D.C. Council more than a year earlier. In an Aug. 6, 2025, letter, she urged lawmakers to overhaul the Youth Rehabilitation Act, citing a separate case in which another 19-year-old received probation after shooting someone in the chest aboard a Metrobus.

SENATOR TIM SHEEHY: SOFT-ON-CRIME JUDGES NEED CONSEQUENCES. THE JAIL ACT DELIVERS

The law, which the D.C. Council expanded in 2018, allows eligible offenders who committed crimes before turning 25 to receive sentences below otherwise applicable mandatory minimums and potentially have their convictions set aside, Pirro wrote. Murder and the most serious sexual abuse offenses are excluded.

In that separate case described in the 2025 letter, the 19-year-old pleaded guilty to two offenses carrying five-year mandatory minimums but received probation after four months in jail awaiting trial, according to Pirro’s letter.

SUSPECTED FLORIDA PUBLIX SLASHER WALKED FREE FROM COURT MONTHS EARLIER DESPITE VICTIM WARNINGS

"This sentence was a legal sentence only because he was sentenced under the YRA," she wrote.

Pirro argued the law needed changes to balance rehabilitation with accountability. Her office said 96% of defendants younger than 25 who received felony sentences in D.C. Superior Court from 2022 through 2024 were eligible for sentencing under the act.

FBI REPORTS 114% JUMP IN VIOLENT CRIME ARRESTS UNDER TRUMP COMPARED TO BIDEN’S FINAL MONTHS

The White House pointed to Trump’s Safe and Beautiful Task Force as its response to crime in the capital, saying the operation has made more than 19,000 arrests, including those of murderers, sex offenders, drug traffickers and other violent criminals.

Fox News Digital reached out to the D.C. Council and Judge Di Toro’s office for comment.

item.title: Common blood pressure drug helps more stroke survivors reach critical health target
item.description: The REDUCE trial found spironolactone lowered blood pressure by nearly eight points in stroke survivors, but key questions about prevention remain.
item.content:encoded:
A low-cost medication could help stroke survivors whose blood pressure remains elevated despite treatment, a new study suggests.

The research, known as the REDUCE trial, looked at whether adding spironolactone, a medication commonly known as a water pill, could help lower blood pressure after a stroke. The findings were presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions, Nov. 6-9, 2026, in Chicago.

Participants were split into two groups. One added spironolactone to their regular treatment, while the other continued with usual post-stroke care.

SIMPLE EXERCISE DONE JUST ONCE A WEEK COULD HELP LOWER BLOOD PRESSURE

Researchers tracked the participants' blood pressure at home over the following six months to determine whether adding the medication made a difference.

After three months, the top blood pressure number was nearly eight points lower on average among people taking spironolactone compared with those receiving usual care – about 126 versus 133, the study said.

More patients taking spironolactone also reached the recommended blood pressure goal of less than 130/80. That included 52% of those taking the medication compared with 30% receiving usual care.

"Lowering blood pressure is the most important step in preventing another stroke, yet many survivors struggle to reach recommended blood pressure targets after a stroke," study co-lead author Dr. Jordana Cohen, an associate professor of medicine and epidemiology at the University of Pennsylvania, said in a news release.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"When spironolactone was added to post-stroke care, we saw a meaningful drop in blood pressure that may lower the risk of future strokes and heart attacks," she added.

Dr. Alfred Joshua, a California-based board-certified emergency physician and former chief medical officer who was not involved in the research, said the findings are encouraging, but do not yet show that the medication prevents a subsequent stroke.

"We already know that controlling blood pressure lowers the risk of another stroke," Joshua told Fox News Digital. "This study measured blood pressure, so whether adding spironolactone leads to fewer repeat strokes is still an open question."

Spironolactone works by helping the body get rid of extra salt and water, which can lower blood pressure, according to the U.S. National Library of Medicine. It also causes the body to hold onto potassium, so patients taking it need to have their levels checked, the drug’s prescribing information states.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Joshua warned that high potassium is one of the main safety concerns because it can develop without symptoms. The risk can be higher for people with kidney problems and those taking certain medications or potassium supplements.

The medication can also lower blood pressure enough to cause dizziness, he added.

"If your blood pressure is still high after a stroke, bring your home readings to your clinician and ask whether this medication is a good fit," Joshua advised.

The trial ended early with 160 participants instead of the planned 200, and about 15% did not have blood pressure readings available at the three-month mark, the researchers noted.

People taking spironolactone were also taking slightly more blood pressure medications overall than those receiving usual care.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The study was not designed to determine whether spironolactone actually prevents another stroke or heart attack. Larger and longer studies are needed to answer that question, according to the researchers.

Fox News Digital reached out to the researchers for comment.

item.title: Charlamagne blasts AOC for ‘beating around the bush,’ presses progressives on backing Hakeem Jeffries
item.description: Charlamagne tha God called out Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for dodging a direct challenge to Hakeem Jeffries' speaker of the House bid.
item.content:encoded:
Radio host Charlamagne tha God blasted Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., for "beating around the bush" about House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries' bid for speaker on Friday — criticizing her explanation of leadership elections instead of directly calling for a challenger.

"I'm watching a lot of beating around the bush. When I see AOC do her tutorial on Instagram Live and I see her getting asked questions … What she really wants to say is, ‘I don’t think Hakeem Jeffrey should be the speaker,'" Charlamagne said during Friday’s episode of the Loud Speakers Network's "The Brilliant Idiots" podcast.

"But, instead of just coming out and saying that and saying, 'Hey, I don't think he should be the speaker of the House. Somebody should challenge him,' she's kind of like beating around the bush telling people why, you know, what the process would look like," he continued. "We don't need a civics lesson."

REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: A USER’S MANUAL TO UPCOMING LEADERSHIP ELECTIONS IN THE HOUSE AND SENATE

The debate over Jeffries' bid has extended beyond podcast commentary to incoming lawmakers weighing their votes. 

Rep.-elect Adam Hamawy, D-N.J., said his support should not be taken for granted.

"We're not withholding votes," Hamawy said. "What we’re doing is saying we're undecided. We’re not going to rubber-stamp anything."

Other Democrats have expressed firm support for Jeffries. Rep. Wesley Bell, D-Mo., a Congressional Black Caucus member, left no uncertainty about his choice.

"Hakeem Jeffries all the way," Bell said, in a statement to Fox News Digital.

WHOOPI GOLDBERG LECTURES DEMOCRATS OVER INFIGHTING ABOUT LEADERSHIP, WARNS 'GET YOUR STUFF TOGETHER'

Charlamagne's assessment followed a social media clip, in which Ocasio-Cortez explained how lawmakers enter leadership races. She encouraged viewers to ask whom their representatives supported rather than simply whether they opposed a particular candidate.

"The question needs to be, ‘Who do you actually want for the speakership? Who is running?’ And right now, both of these races are uncontested," Ocasio-Cortez said.

Charlamagne challenged whether that procedural explanation addressed progressives' disagreements with Jeffries, particularly over military assistance to Israel, and questioned how lawmakers who have described Israel’s actions in Gaza as genocide could support leaders they believe would continue those policies.

"We need, ‘Hey, AOC, simple and plain. As a person, who has said Israel is committing a genocide in Gaza, how can you support leaders that you know who continue to support, in your words, the genocide?’" Charlamagne said.

VAN HOLLEN CHALLENGES SCHUMER FOR SENATE LEADERSHIP AFTER DEMOCRATIC ELECTION SWEEP

Ocasio-Cortez was among the lawmakers listed on a November 2025 resolution, seeking recognition of genocide in Gaza.

Jeffries, who announced his speaker candidacy after the midterms, addressed divisions over Israel assistance during an interview on Wednesday, saying that lawmakers would work together to reconsider how assistance is provided.

"Clearly, dramatic change is necessary," Jeffries said. "I've repeatedly made that point clear, including in July in a letter to the Caucus."

Fox News Digital reached out to the offices of AOC, Jeffries and Schumer for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Blood, staples and Nintendo Power Glove: Texas Death match gets gnarly as Full Gear sees new champions crowned
item.description: Austin Creed smashed Brody King with a Nintendo Power Glove in the AEW World Trios Championship Texas Death match that delivered pure brutality.
item.content:encoded:
Blood, guts, staples and a Nintendo Power Glove. It’s a Texas Death match. Did you expect anything else?

Something had to give with the All Elite Wrestling World Trios Championship on the line. Adam Page, Bandido and Brody King were set to defend their titles with all their might against Swerve Strickland, Kofi and Austin Creed. Kofi and Creed came into the match with a little anxiety – having no real interest in getting bloodied up when the match was first announced.

But Kofi and Creed – who probably weren’t used to the brutality of what a match could bring – gave it their all to help Strickland grab the championship. For the second time in the group’s history, they have the AEW World Trios Championship around their waists.

There were incredible moments in the match and some that made you shield your eyes.

Creed is a noted video game nerd. Who isn’t? But Creed went all the way back to 1989 to pull out something that did damage to King – the Nintendo Power Glove.

The device was kept in a bag that Stokely Hathaway was holding. He called for the duffle bag and pulled out the piece of gaming equipment. It was a thrill to see Creed use his creativity and take it to a, dare I say, new level.

After King bullied him while trying to get the Power Glove wrapped around his wrist, Creed punched the brute in the face and it exploded. No Nintendo Entertainment System necessary.

It looked like it hurt a bit but it was probably the most creative spot of the match. Creed also used a barbed-wire-laden trombone to do some damage to his counterparts earlier in the match.

Kofi dropping the boom on Adam Page – more like Adam Pane, am I right? I have some jokes in my back pocket sometimes.

Anyways, Kofi and Creed put two windowpanes on Page as the wrestler was sprawled out on about a half-dozen chairs. Kofi went to the barricade and hit the Boom Drop on Page, breaking the glass all over Page’s torso.

It was interesting to see Kofi get hardcore. He opened the door to something deeper inside of him and it showed. The glass shattered across the ground outside the ring, while Strickland, Kofi and Creed took control of the match.

The way fighters and wrestlers are described in the ring is going "toe-to-toe" or "nose-to-nose." It’s never really staplegun-to-staplegun unless Page and Strickland are involved in a match.

Strickland asked Page to sit down with him – not for a conversation, but for some brutality. Page obliged and the two, with stapleguns in their hands, they used them on each other’s bodies. When their teammates got into the ring, they each received staples for their troubles.

It would not be the last time the two rivals would go for it all in the match. Something much worse came later.

It was a callback to their Texas Death match at Full Gear in 2023, as Fightful pointed out during the night. Page busted Strickland open and with blood pouring out of his face, Page opened his mouth to get a taste.

This time, it was Strickland who made the gnarliest of decisions to get a taste of Page’s blood. The spot may have divided social media but the storyline and the opportunity was there – Strickland took full advantage.

Page did have the upper hand for a brief moment after the gross moment. But as Page went to slug Strickland with a chair shot, he was stopped dead in his tracks. Strickland was smiling. Page thought he had the match in the bag. He was setting up Strickland for a string of Buckshot Lariats. He only hit two of them. On the third, Strickland countered. He gave Page a House Call, knocking out his opponent.

item.title: DHS chief Mullin says Iran poses daily threat to Trump and his family amid drone concerns
item.description: Markwayne Mullin says Trump and his family are Iran's top target, revealing daily threat briefings as drone security gaps raise urgent concerns.
item.content:encoded:
Department of Homeland Security (DHS) chief Markwayne Mullin warned that President Donald Trump and his family remain top targets of threats from Iran, saying on "The Sunday Briefing" that officials receive intelligence about potential threats daily as concerns grow over the use of drones.

"Well, every single day during our presidential briefings, we receive aspirational threats from Iran. We know that President Trump — and his family — is target number one," Mullin said.

Mullin's remarks came amid questions about a report alleging Israeli intelligence had identified a potential Iranian plot involving explosive-laden drones targeting Trump. While he did not confirm the specific report, Mullin said officials were aware of threats.

Mullin also called countering unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) his "number one issue," citing increasingly sophisticated drone technology, cartel activity along the southern border and vulnerabilities at major public gatherings.

US MILITARY TOOK DOWN APPROXIMATELY 100 SUSPECTED CARTEL DRONES AT SOUTHERN BORDER IN AUGUST

"Our counter-UAS measures need help, and DHS is leading that, because we encounter more drones on our southern border because of the cartels and the fight we're having with them every single day trying to get drugs into the United States. And we're seeing new technologies that we're having a hard time defeating right now," he continued.

Mexican cartels are reported to be using commercial and modified drones to watch U.S. security personnel, map patrol routines and support smuggling corridors along the southern border as authorities expand efforts to disable the aircraft.

US MILITARY BASES ARE ‘ILL-EQUIPPED’ TO STOP DRONE SWARMS, TOP COMMANDER REVEALS AFTER RUBIO'S UAP WARNING

The U.S. military detected 378 drone incursions along the border during the previous 30 days, Brig. Gen. Brian Filler of Joint Task Force-Southern Border told reporters. He said the trend was increasing, and the aircraft were typically commercial drones with cameras used for surveillance tied to smuggling and human trafficking.

Mullin said drone threats extend well beyond the southern border, pointing to security concerns at major sporting events and other large gatherings.

During the FIFA World Cup, for instance, Mullin said law enforcement encountered more than 2,000 drones, confiscated 700 and made multiple arrests. He noted that Los Angeles will host the Olympics in 2028.

But the DHS secretary warned that drone security is also needed at everyday gatherings, including high school football games, parades and professional sporting events.

"There are holes in our counter-UAS ability to be kinetic and bring down real threats," Mullin said, adding that he was coordinating with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on the matter due to issues of airspace clearance.

Mullin said he has established a dedicated counter-drone department within DHS as the agency works to address gaps in its ability to neutralize potential threats.

Fox News Digital's Armando Regil Velasco contributed to this report.

item.title: Beauty queen stripped of Miss USA crown over hidden husband, kids gets unexpected spotlight decades later
item.description: Justus Kelley honors Mary Leona Gage, who lost her Miss USA crown in 1957 for being married with children, as she prepares for Miss Universe.
item.content:encoded:
Nearly 70 years ago, a beauty queen lost her Miss USA crown after pageant officials learned she was married and had children. In August, Justus Kelley broke that barrier, becoming the first married woman and mother to win the title during the pageant's 75th edition.

Kelley, 31, is a foster mother who founded the nonprofit Foster Footprints to support children and families involved in foster care.

The historic victory came three years after the Miss USA pageant changed its rules to allow married women and mothers to compete.

Kelley is scheduled to compete in the 75th Miss Universe pageant, which is set to take place Nov. 24 in Puerto Rico.

FORMER MISS USA CONTESTANT MADE A LIFE-CHANGING DECISION AT 26 AFTER CANCER DEVASTATED FAMILY

Kelley paid tribute to Gage by wearing a custom black-and-white coat featuring the former beauty queen's image as she traveled to Puerto Rico for the competition.

"Having the opportunity to represent the United States on the Miss Universe stage, I couldn't help but think about Mary Leona Gage and the circumstances under which she represented this organization," Kelley, 31, told People magazine.

"She was a woman who, in many ways, wasn't allowed to be fully herself or embrace all that she was. Her title was ultimately taken away because society wasn't ready to accept who she was as a wife and mother of two."

On Aug. 27, the Miss USA Organization held the 75th edition of the national pageant in Miami. Kelley, who held the title of Miss Virginia USA 2026, succeeded 2025 winner Audrey Eckert. The pageant began allowing married women and mothers to compete in 2023.

WATCH: MISS USA 2026 REVEALS HOW SHE TRAINED FOR PAGEANT WITH KIDS IN TOW

In 1957, Gage represented Maryland in the Miss USA pageant and won the title, according to People.

Shortly after Gage's win, rumors circulated about her marital status and children. Gage initially denied the reports. However, it was later revealed that she had married at 14 and given birth to her first child soon afterward. She had her second child at 16, The Baltimore Sun reported.

Gage also misrepresented her age, telling pageant officials she was 21 when she was actually 18.

Following an official investigation, Gage was disqualified and stripped of her Miss USA crown. Runner-up Charlotte Sheffield, who represented Utah, assumed the crown and received the prizes.

Gage, who lost the crown about 24 hours after her win, said she received hate mail following her disqualification.

Gage had already competed in the Miss Universe preliminary round and secured a spot among the 15 semifinalists before she was disqualified. Although Sheffield inherited the Miss USA crown, she could not replace Gage in the international competition because preliminary judging had already concluded.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

According to The Baltimore Sun, Gage later worked as a performer at the Tropicana Hotel in Las Vegas and reportedly dated Frank Sinatra and former Mr. Universe Mickey Hargitay. She also pursued a film career but never achieved widespread success.

Despite losing her crown, Gage continued watching the Miss USA pageant every year. She died in 2010 at age 71.

Kelley told People that Gage has been on her mind as she prepares for the Miss Universe competition.

"I think about how much has changed since then, and how grateful I am that today's American women have the opportunity to represent their country while embracing every part of who they are," Kelley said.

"I hope this moment serves as a reminder that we stand on the shoulders of women who dared to challenge what was expected of them, so that we could have the freedom to be exactly who we are today."

The Miss USA pageant began in 1952 in Long Beach, California, with New York's Jackie Loughery becoming its first winner. The competition is separate from the Miss America pageant, which traces its history to a 1921 event in Atlantic City, New Jersey.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

In an earlier interview with Fox News Digital, Kelley expressed a similar message about motherhood and ambition.

She said she hoped to use her reign as Miss USA to challenge the idea that women must choose between their families, careers and personal dreams.

"You don't have to choose one part of who you are," Kelley said. "You can be all of who you are. That, to me, is the message. We can embrace every part of who we are. It doesn't take away from the other. It doesn't mean there aren't trade-offs, and there aren't times when we have to lean on our village more heavily to get through all the things that we may be pursuing. But know that we don't have to sacrifice ourselves."

Kelley said her victory gave her an opportunity to represent mothers and wives who balance family life with their own ambitions.

"Knowing that history was made as the first mom, as the first wife, as the first woman in her 30s, my first thought was how amazing it is to get to do this and to represent women from all over the country, from all over the world that resonate with, 'Hey, we're still dreaming,'" she said.

"We're raising our families, but we still have dreams. We still have things that we want to go after and pursue. But what an honor. I get to do this. I get to represent these women. What an honor."

item.title: Iran vows ‘we will find you’ to 2 US Navy officers the day warship returns from Middle East
item.description: Iran's embassy in South Africa posted a "We will find you" threat targeting two USS Spruance officers as the destroyer returned to San Diego.
item.content:encoded:
Iran’s embassy in South Africa threatened two U.S. Navy officers with a "We will find you" message online as their warship returned to San Diego on Friday after a historic 357-day deployment that included combat against Iranian forces.

The warning, posted on X on Nov. 13 alongside images identifying the USS Spruance’s commanding officer and executive officer, prompted a regional expert to warn that Iran’s public targeting of American service members should set off alarm bells in Washington.

The embassy identified Cmdr. Leigh R. Tate, commanding officer of the Spruance, and Lt. Cmdr. Jeffrey E. York, the ship’s executive officer.

IRAN MINES US TROOPS' SOCIAL MEDIA AS MILITARY CONSIDERS SEIZING CELLPHONES

"We will find you," the embassy wrote on X.

The embassy had previously singled out the officers in a March 28 post accusing them of ordering Tomahawk missile launches that killed 168 children at an elementary school in Minab, Iran.

"Remember these two criminals," the earlier post began. "Don’t they have children of their own?" the embassy asked at the time.

Behnam Ben Taleblu, a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, warned that the rhetoric coming out of Tehran should be taken seriously given Iran’s history of plotting attacks against American officials.

"This should be setting off alarm bells in Washington, in the White House, the Pentagon, and even within CENTCOM," Taleblu told Fox News Digital. "The Islamic Republic has literally identified personnel that they allege are involved in strikes against the regime, and they’re talking about retribution."

"If indeed there is any plot to go after these individuals, it is critical they’re detected, they are disrupted, they are defeated," Taleblu warned.

IRAN-BACKED TERROR SUSPECTS PLOTTED ATTACK ON US TROOPS USING VANS PACKED WITH FUEL, DOJ SAYS

The threat from Iran came a day after President Donald Trump warned Tehran against assassinating senior American officials.

During a Nov. 12 interview with radio host Hugh Hewitt, Trump was asked what would happen if Iran killed a senior U.S. official.

"They will not exist very long, any longer," Trump responded.

His warning also followed reports that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had relocated from his Washington-area residence to a military base amid Iranian threats against his life.

Bessent confirmed the move during a Friday interview on CNBC, saying he was following Secret Service instructions.

"Why am I going to be afraid when the brave military personnel in the Gulf, President Trump, constantly receive death threats?" Bessent asked.

Bessent described Iran as behaving "like a dangerous cornered animal" and insisted the threats would not derail the administration’s economic pressure campaign against Tehran.

TRUMP ADMIN THREATENS IRAN WITH 'CONSEQUENCES' AS ALLIES CONVENE AMID THREATS OF POST-ELECTION ESCALATION

Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and senior White House official Stephen Miller have also reportedly moved into military or other protected housing amid security concerns.

In another post on X, the Iranian embassy in South Africa went on to mock senior administration officials over their security arrangements.

"Rubio, Bessent, Hegseth, and other U.S. officials live in constant fear, haunted by the crimes committed, and now confined to military bunkers for their own protection," the embassy wrote, suggesting they should occasionally appear in public.

The threats come as federal authorities have announced developments in alleged Iranian-backed plots targeting Americans.

On Nov. 10, the FBI added Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps operative Shahram Poursafi to its Most Wanted Terrorists list over an alleged assassination plot targeting former senior U.S. officials, including former national security adviser John Bolton.

That same day, the Justice Department announced terrorism charges against three men accused of involvement in nearly 20 attacks and attempted attacks across Europe and the United States, including an alleged plot targeting a British air base housing American forces.

The developments followed an Oct. 23 U.S. intelligence warning that Iranian efforts to target American personnel abroad had substantially increased, with some plots reaching advanced stages.

TRUMP'S TOP OFFICIALS RETREAT BEHIND MILITARY GATES AS EX-FBI DEPUTY POINTS TO WHAT'S FUELING THREATS

The embassy’s warning coincided with the Spruance’s return to Naval Base San Diego on Nov. 13, ending the longest deployment by a U.S. Navy destroyer since World War II.

The Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer departed San Diego on Nov. 21, 2025, alongside the USS Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group. Its deployment was extended as American forces conducted Operation Epic Fury against Iran.

The Spruance traveled more than 88,000 nautical miles during the deployment and launched dozens of Tomahawk land-attack cruise missiles against Iranian military targets between February and August 2026, according to a statement released by the Navy.

The ship also destroyed 12 unmanned aerial vehicles and four anti-ship cruise missiles while operating under persistent threats from Iranian drones and missiles.

"Spruance, in particular, as the alternate air defense commander was, I would say, instrumental in defending the carrier, defending the force from those inbound threats," Tate said Friday in the statement.

CENTCOM COMMANDER TOUTS USS ABRAHAM LINCOLN MENTAL HEALTH RECORD AFTER MORE THAN 260 DAYS WITHOUT PORT CALL

The destroyer also participated in the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports. In April, it intercepted the Iranian-flagged cargo vessel Touska after the ship failed to comply with repeated American warnings.

U.S. Central Command said at the time that the Spruance ordered the vessel’s engine room evacuated before firing rounds that disabled the ship.

Tate called commanding the ship during the extended deployment an "honor of a lifetime."

"Spruance sailors made a difference," Tate also said in a statement Friday. "They represented their families, their ship and the United States Navy with distinction."

Meanwhile, Iranian officials have also been threatening U.S. military installations overseas.

On Nov. 11, Iranian Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei warned that Tehran could strike American bases in Europe if the United States resumed attacks on Iran.

ANOTHER TRUMP HEAVYWEIGHT REVEALED TO BE LIVING ON MILITARY BASE AS CABINET ROSTER GROWS

"If the Americans make a mistake and attack us, we will not limit ourselves to nearby bases," Rezaei told Al Mayadeen.

Taleblu described the embassy’s latest statements as part of an escalating pattern of threats against American personnel.

"This is an escalation of the course that we’ve been on," he said, pointing to threatening rhetoric from Iranian diplomatic accounts and hard-line commentators during and after the war.

"So this is basically incitement and invective from the world’s foremost state sponsor of terrorism, one which unfortunately has a track record of carrying these things out, even with a delay."

He pointed to threats against U.S. military personnel following the accidental American shootdown of an Iranian civilian airliner in 1988.

"Something like this is not unprecedented in the 47-year shadow war between the Islamic Republic and America," Taleblu said, warning that the conflict has increasingly moved from covert operations into open warfare and increasing public threats on social media.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Pentagon and the White House for comment.

item.title: Retro burger chain once served up beloved TV character to American diners
item.description: Before Dunkin' ever became a coffee empire, founder William Rosenberg built Howdy Beef N' Burger around the Howdy Doody puppet with about 30 locations.
item.content:encoded:
Before Dunkin' became a household name for coffee and donuts, its founder tried to build a fast-food business around a TV puppet.

William Rosenberg, who founded Dunkin' Donuts, launched Howdy Beef N' Burger in New England in 1961. At its peak, the chain had about 30 locations, some of which operated alongside Dunkin' Donuts. 

The retro chain was originally called Howdy Beefburger before changing to Howdy Beef N’ Burger, according to reports.

RETRO PIZZA HUT DRAWS CUSTOMERS FROM HOURS AWAY AS 1980S NOSTALGIA SENDS SALES SOARING

The regional chain took its name and mascot from Howdy Doody, the beloved cowboy marionette who starred in a children's show that aired on NBC from 1947 to 1960, according to food website Chowhound. 

The show featured the puppet and human characters in skits and songs before a studio audience of children known as the "peanut gallery."

Aside from burgers and fries, the chain also served a signature Big "B" burger.

It also served roast beef sandwiches, fried chicken, shakes and New England seafood dishes such as clam strips, chowder and lobster rolls, according to the food history blog Burger Beast.

FAST-FOOD CHAIN THAT ONCE LIT UP AMERICAN ROADS STILL MISSED DECADES LATER

Promotions leaned into the chain’s family appeal. A Boston Globe ad, cited by The Takeout, promised diners could "feed the family on just pocket change." 

The chain also offered burger deals and prizes, giveaways and buttons for children, according to reports.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

But Howdy's reportedly faced competition from McDonald’s, plus Rosenberg’s company had other ventures to manage, including seafood, pancakes and deli businesses. 

When his son Robert became company president in 1963, he began narrowing the company’s focus to Dunkin’ Donuts, Chowhound reported.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

While Dunkin' continued to grow, Howdy's faded, with some locations sold off to other restaurant chains. 

A Quincy, Massachusetts, restaurant became a Wendy’s in 1979, according to Burger Beast.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

By the 1980s, the chain had largely disappeared, according to Chowhound. 

Today, the New England burger chain survives in vintage ads, nostalgic memorabilia and diners' memories.

Howdy Doody wasn’t the only fictional character to inspire a restaurant, though.

Bubba Gump Shrimp Co. draws on the 1994 film "Forrest Gump," while Central Perk Coffee Co. recreates the café from the series "Friends." 

Meanwhile, Tony Soprano’s, an East Coast pizza chain, is themed around "The Sopranos," according to The Takeout.
